acceptedFindings.title: Manuscript reports linear model but actual method is quantile regression
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Incorrect model family misleads interpretation; readers might think coefficients represent mean change rather than median change.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Correct the manuscript to state quantile regression (median) and interpret coefficients accordingly.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: stats-run.json method field is 'quantile-regression'; manuscript.md 'Methods' states 'The detected model family was linear'.

acceptedFindings.title: Unbound exploratory analysis presented as confirmatory
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The run is not bound to a method-selection artifact or analysis spec, so p-values and CIs cannot be interpreted as confirmatory. Presenting them as precise (p=0.0000) misleads about the strength of evidence.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Either bind the analysis to a pre-specified protocol (method-selection + AnalysisSpec) and rerun, or clearly label the entire report as exploratory and suppress p-values/overinterpretation.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: stats-run.json binding.status is 'unbound'; resultPosture.supports includes only 'local data debugging', not paper-ready conclusions.

acceptedFindings.title: Analysis is unbound and exploratory, but presented as a final-stage manuscript
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Unbound runs lack pre-specified analysis plans, increasing risk of p-hacking and overinterpretation. Claims should be clearly exploratory.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Either bind the analysis to a pre-registered AnalysisSpec/method selection, or explicitly label the entire manuscript as dataset-level exploration with no inferential intent.

acceptedFindings.title: Missing specification of quantile in quantile regression
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without specifying the quantile (e.g., 0.5 for median), the target of the model is ambiguous and irreproducible.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add the quantile value (presumably 0.5) to methods and results.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: No 'quantile' parameter in stats-run.json parameters; manuscript title says 'median' but methods omitted.

acceptedFindings.title: No variable definitions or cohort construction details provided
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Cannot assess data plausibility, confounding, or external validity; missingness handling not described.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Include a data dictionary, cohort flow chart, and description of missing data patterns. If no missing data, confirm explicitly.

acceptedFindings.title: No analysis code or data provided for external reproducibility
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The manuscript mentions reproducibility but only has artifacts; without code, exact steps cannot be verified.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide the analysis script or detailed computational steps, and ideally the raw data (if PHI allows) or a synthetic version.

acceptedFindings.title: Model family misreported as 'linear' instead of quantile regression
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md (Methods: 'The detected model family was linear.')
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Readers may assume ordinary least squares regression, leading to misinterpretation of assumptions, estimates, and standard errors.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Replace 'linear' with 'quantile regression (median)' in the manuscript's methods and specify the quantile estimated.

acceptedFindings.title: Missingness handling not reported
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Complete-case analysis may introduce bias if missingness is non-random. No information on exclusion counts or patterns is provided.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a missing data flow diagram or table, report missingness per variable, consider sensitivity analysis (e.g., multiple imputation).
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: No missingness table or counts found in artifacts.

acceptedFindings.title: Variable definitions and units missing
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Interpretation of effect sizes (e.g., treatment estimate 1.31, age 0.14) is impossible without knowing measurement units and variable meanings.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide explicit definitions, units, and coding schemes for outcome, treatment, age, severity. Include descriptive statistics.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Manuscript states 'The primary outcome, exposure, and covariates were not fully encoded in the text report'.

acceptedFindings.title: Standard error estimation method and model assumptions unstated
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Quantile regression inference requires correct standard error estimation (e.g., bootstrap, rank inversion). Without knowing the method, the validity of p-values and CIs cannot be assessed.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Document the standard error computation method used (e.g., from statsmodels default), justify its appropriateness, and consider providing bootstrap confidence intervals as sensitivity.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: No parameter or documentation in diagnostics.json or stats-run.json describing the SE method.

acceptedFindings.title: Shapiro-Wilk test applied to quantile regression residuals is inappropriate
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Shapiro-Wilk tests normality, which is not an assumption of quantile regression. Reporting it may confuse validity checks.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Remove Shapiro-Wilk from quantile regression diagnostics and report more appropriate diagnostics (e.g., quantile-specific residual plots, pseudo R-squared).

acceptedFindings.title: P-values reported as 0.0000 for const
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: P-values should not be reported as zero; it violates precision standards and can mislead about certainty.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report p-values using '< 0.001' or scientific notation, e.g., 3.71e-19.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: manuscript.md shows 'p=0.0000' for const; stats-run.json p_value is 3.71433e-19.

acceptedFindings.title: P-values reported as exactly 0.0000
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md (Results: p=0.0000 for const and severity)
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: P-values are never exactly zero; reporting '0.0000' suggests perfect certainty, which is misleading. Scientific notation or 'p < 0.0001' is more accurate.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Replace 'p=0.0000' with actual p-value in scientific notation (e.g., p = 3.7e-19) or p < 0.0001 as appropriate.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: stats-run.json shows p_value: 3.714334661542577e-19 for const, not zero.

acceptedFindings.title: Self-referential limitations contain placeholder/inaccurate statements
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The document says 'No reader-facing paper/manuscript artifact was found' and 'No reader-facing report was available for claim alignment' while being the manuscript itself. This undermines credibility.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Remove or revise those sentences to reflect the actual presence of the manuscript. Ensure limitations are about the study, not metadata of the review process.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Manifestly contradictory: manuscript.md exists but the text denies its existence.

acceptedFindings.title: No literature context or references provided
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: A complete research report should situate the analysis within existing knowledge, even if only to note it is a local exploration without comparative benchmarks.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a brief introduction or discussion referencing prior work on similar outcomes or treatments, or explicitly state the analysis is not compared to external literature.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: No references section or in-text citations found.

acceptedFindings.title: No sensitivity analysis or confounding adjustment description
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Observational study without discussion of confounders limits causal interpretations even at local level.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Include a DAG or explicit list of confounders, and if possible, a sensitivity analysis (e.g., E-value) to acknowledge unmeasured confounding.
